# Linux sandbox driver build

The `linux-sbx` branch of this fork is an upstream Cua Driver release plus a
few patch commits. `cluster_build.sh` turns it into a signed Linux x86_64
release on one Linux build host: no CI, and no GitHub workflow runs in this
fork (the branch deletes upstream's). Where the release is published (the
branch and tag pushed here, the archives uploaded to an artifact store) is the
build host's own job and is not in this repository.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `cluster_build.sh` | The whole build, in order; prints the release directory last |
| `select_upstream_tag.sh` | Highest stable `cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z` tag upstream |
| `next_prerelease_tag.sh` | `cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z-linux-sbx.<N>` candidate, one past the highest tag here |
| `rebase_onto_tag.sh` | Replay the patch commits onto that tag; drops generated commits; exit 10 on conflict |
| `rebase_probe.sh` | The same replay onto upstream `main`, nothing pushed: early warning of next week's conflict |
| `prune_upstream_workflows.sh` | Generated commit that deletes every file under `.github/workflows/` |
| `make_source_bundle.sh` | `git bundle` of the rebased branch (above the tag) and `linux-sbx-metadata.txt` |
| `metadata.sh` | Strict reader for the metadata file (never sourced) |
| `debian11_rootfs.sh` | Debian 11 build root (debootstrap, sha256-pinned downloads, cached tarball) |
| `apt_bootstrap.sh` | Build packages inside that root: frozen snapshot, archive mirror as fallback |
| `debian11_proot.sh` | Run a command in the root under proot (no container runtime needed) |
| `checkout_from_bundle.sh` | Build source taken from the bundle, checked against the metadata |
| `pack_linux_artifact.sh` | Full and `-binary` archives, `SHA256SUMS`, `--smoke` start of the packaged CLI |
| `bridge_tests.sh` | Release gate: the extension bridge's tests on the rebased tree; exit 11 on failure |
| `assemble_release.sh` | Build output + bundle into one directory, cross-checked |
| `sign_release_assets.sh` | cosign signature per asset (`--key`: key pair, offline) |

Every decision lives in these scripts, so each can be run and tested by hand.

## Building a release

```
cluster_build.sh --work DIR --key cosign.key [--mirror-env FILE] [--upstream-tag cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z]
```

Needs Linux x86_64, NOPASSWD sudo (debootstrap and the build root are
root-owned), git, curl and cosign. `DIR` keeps the rootfs cache and one
directory per run (`DIR/runs/<run id>/`). Exit 0 with the release in
`DIR/runs/<id>/release`, 10 on a rebase conflict (report in
`DIR/runs/<id>/out/linux-sbx-rebase-conflict.md`), 11 when the bridge tests
fail on the rebased tree (nothing signed; the failures are in
`DIR/runs/<id>/build.log`), 1 otherwise.

`--mirror-env FILE` names download proxies, one `KEY=VALUE` per line, for hosts
where the upstream servers are slow or unreachable. The file is parsed, not
sourced, and only the keys listed in `cluster_build.sh --help` are accepted.
Every download is still checked by sha256 pins, the Debian keyring and
`Cargo.lock`, so a proxy changes where bytes come from, not what is built.

## What a build does

1. **Select.** Lists `refs/tags/cua-driver-rs-v*` upstream and picks the highest
   `X.Y.Z` (or `--upstream-tag`). A prerelease suffix (`-rc.1`) or another
   component's tag is never picked.
2. **Name.** Computes the `cua-driver-rs-v<version>-linux-sbx.<N>` candidate from
   the tags already in this repository.
3. **Rebase.** The patch commits are the commits on `linux-sbx` that no stable
   upstream release tag reaches. Commits carrying the `Linux-Sbx-Generated:`
   trailer are dropped; the rest are replayed onto the tag. A conflict writes a
   report and stops with exit 10.
4. **Prune.** One generated commit deletes every file under
   `.github/workflows/`, so upstream's release and CI workflows never register
   or run here once the branch is pushed. The commit is reproducible (bot
   identity, dates from its parent): an unchanged week yields the same sha. It
   is dropped and regenerated by the next rebase, so it never conflicts with
   upstream's workflow edits.
5. **Bundle.** `git bundle` of the branch above the upstream tag, plus
   `linux-sbx-metadata.txt`: upstream tag and sha, rebased sha, the branch sha the
   build started from, bundle sha256, prerelease tag candidate, run id.
6. **Build.** Debian 11 root under proot, so glibc 2.31 is the floor: the
   binaries run on Debian 11+ and Ubuntu 20.04+, as upstream's `debian:11`
   container build. The source comes out of the bundle (upstream tag fetched
   publicly, bundle verified, sha checked). Release build, Node runtime,
   archives, smoke test.
7. **Gate.** `bridge_tests.sh` in the same root, same target and profile:
   the extension bridge (frames, host, listener, peer, endpoint, engine tests
   against a fake extension), the CDP wire it runs over, the Linux adapter's
   hook guard and the native host CLI. A rebase that applies cleanly can still
   break the bridge (a new DevTools port path upstream, a changed
   demultiplexer); this is where that stops the release, with exit 11.
8. **Sign.** Cross-checks build output against the bundle and metadata, then
   signs every archive and `SHA256SUMS` with the cosign key pair
   (`<file>.sigstore.json`, offline: nothing goes to the public transparency
   log). The bundle and the metadata are not signed: the metadata records the
   bundle's sha256, which `checkout_from_bundle.sh` and the publisher check.

## Publishing

`cluster_build.sh` pushes and uploads nothing. The publisher, on the build
host, checks the release (metadata, bundle sha256, `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`,
`cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub --insecure-ignore-tlog=true` for every
signed file), uploads it, then pushes the rebased sha to `linux-sbx` only if
the branch is still the metadata's `previous_sha`
(`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/linux-sbx:<previous_sha>`), and tags it with
the prerelease tag. A week where upstream has no new release and the branch did
not move rebuilds the same sha and has nothing to push.

## Patch layout

The patch commits are kept in this order, so a conflict has one place to land:

1. `ci(linux-sbx)` commits: this directory only.
2. Commits that only **add** files (the bridge under
   `browser/ext_bridge/`, `browser/wire.rs`, their tests). They cannot
   conflict with upstream.
3. One `linux-sbx seam` commit, last: every edit to a file upstream owns
   (module declarations, the CDP wire switch and dial branches, the native
   host entry in `main.rs`, the Linux adapter's hooks and their guard). Keep it
   small and keep it last; a change to an upstream file goes into it, not
   into a new commit.

The pushed head always carries one more commit on top of the three: the
generated `ci(linux-sbx): remove upstream workflows in this fork`
(`prune_upstream_workflows.sh`). `linux-sbx` is this fork's default branch, and
GitHub runs scheduled upstream workflows from it: a push without that commit
re-registers 176 of them, which then fail daily for lack of upstream's secrets.
`rebase_onto_tag.sh` drops and regenerates it, so a rebuilt branch has it again
automatically; a branch built by hand needs it before it is pushed.

The guard in the Linux adapter (`ext_bridge_hook_tests`) lists every method of
`impl BrowserPlatform for LinuxBrowserPlatform` as either hooked or not
needing a hook, with the reason. A method upstream adds fails the gate until
someone decides which it is.

## Early warning

```
rebase_probe.sh --dir DIR --repo https://github.com/yanyaoer/cua.git \
    --upstream-url https://github.com/trycua/cua [--conflict-report FILE]
```

Replays the patch commits onto upstream's `main` in a clone kept in `DIR` and
reports `result=clean` or `result=conflict` with the stopped commit and the
files (exit 0 or 10). Nothing is pushed or built. Run it daily: a conflict on
`main` usually reaches a release tag days later, and resolving it by hand
before then keeps the weekly release on schedule.

## Resolving a conflict

```
git fetch origin linux-sbx
git fetch https://github.com/trycua/cua tag cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z
git switch linux-sbx
git rebase -i cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z  # drop the Linux-Sbx-Generated commit; resolve, then git rebase --continue
git push --force-with-lease origin linux-sbx
```

The next build regenerates the pruning commit on top.

## Verifying a published archive

```
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
for f in *.tar.gz SHA256SUMS; do
  cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" --insecure-ignore-tlog=true "$f"
done
```

`cosign.pub` is the public half of the build host's key pair; whoever installs
the driver pins it.
